data.final_week_advice: Focus on timed practice and reviewing weak areas like kinetics and equilibrium.
data.summary: This plan prioritizes the student's weak units, Kinetics and Equilibrium, in the first half of the study period. It integrates live classes for these units to reinforce understanding before moving to new material. The final two weeks are dedicated to mixed review and timed practice to simulate exam conditions.

weeks.focus: Master mole calculations and atomic structure fundamentals.
tasks: Complete 20 practice problems on molar mass and stoichiometry (1.1, 4.5).
Analyze 5 mass spectrometry graphs to determine isotopic abundance (1.2).
Write electron configurations for 10 elements including transition metals (1.5).

weeks.focus: Understand reaction rates and rate laws through live instruction.
tasks: Attend live class on Kinetics (5.1, 5.2).
Solve 8 problems calculating initial rates from experimental data (5.1).
Determine rate laws and rate constants for 5 given reactions (5.2).

weeks.focus: Deepen understanding of kinetics with integrated rate laws.
tasks: Graph concentration vs. time for zero, first, and second-order reactions (5.3).
Calculate half-lives for 6 different reaction orders (5.3).
Analyze 4 elementary reaction mechanisms to identify rate-determining steps (5.4).

weeks.focus: Learn equilibrium concepts and reaction quotients.
tasks: Attend live class on Equilibrium (7.1, 7.2, 7.3).
Predict the direction of shift for 5 systems under stress (7.2).
Calculate Q and K for 8 equilibrium systems (7.3, 7.4).

weeks.focus: Review kinetics and equilibrium with mixed practice.
tasks: Do 10 free-response questions on kinetics and mark against scoring guide (5.1-5.4).
Solve 12 equilibrium calculation problems including ICE tables (7.3, 7.4).
Review error analysis from previous weeks and redo 3 missed problems.
Calculate ΔH for 8 reactions using Hess's Law (6.1, 6.2).
Interpret 5 energy diagrams to identify activation energy and enthalpy change (6.2).
Perform calorimetry calculations for 4 specific heat problems (6.4).

weeks.focus: Understand acid-base properties and pH calculations.
tasks: Attend live class on Acids and Bases (8.1, 8.2).
Calculate pH and pOH for 10 strong acid/base solutions (8.2).
Identify conjugate acid-base pairs in 8 chemical equations (8.1).

weeks.focus: Master weak acid/base equilibria and buffers.
tasks: Calculate Ka and Kb for 6 weak acid/base systems (8.3).
Determine pH of 5 buffer solutions using the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation (8.4).
Analyze titration curves for 3 different acid-base systems (8.4).

weeks.focus: Review all units with mixed timed practice.
tasks: Complete a 45-minute timed section of multiple-choice questions covering Units 1-4.
Do 5 free-response questions covering Units 5-9.
Review incorrect answers and create a summary sheet for weak areas.

weeks.focus: Final exam simulation and targeted review.
tasks: Take a full-length practice exam under timed conditions.
Review the exam and redo 10 questions that were incorrect.
Focus review on Kinetics and Equilibrium free-response questions.
